“Unstructured” does not mean that the file contains no organization at all. A JPEG still has an encoding, and an audio file may carry timestamps and metadata; the term concerns how the information is represented for application queries and analysis.

Key points

  • Structured data has a declared record layout, such as a student table with roll number, name and marks; semi-structured data uses self-describing fields or tags.
  • JSON/BSON documents are normally described as semi-structured because their field names convey structure even when different records contain different fields.
  • For large media, an application can store searchable metadata in MongoDB and keep the file in object storage or GridFS; a normal BSON document has a 16 MiB size limit.

Example:

A recorded lecture is unstructured audio content. Its catalogue entry may be a semi-structured document such as {title: "Web Design", durationSeconds: 2400, fileKey: "lecture-01.mp3"}. Searching that entry by title or duration searches metadata, not the spoken words. Full-content search would require an additional process such as transcription and indexing.

This distinction helps prevent the mistaken claim that storing an audio filename automatically makes its audio content queryable by ordinary document fields.

Conclusion: Unstructured data lacks a convenient fixed record schema for its main content, while metadata can still provide a structured or semi-structured way to manage and locate it.

Short 5
Question
Give two features of NoSQL database and explain in brief.
ShortUnit 11.1 Concepts of NoSQL — advantages & features
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Two important NoSQL features are flexible data modelling and horizontal scalability. Flexible modelling accommodates varying record structures; horizontal scalability spreads data or workload across machines to increase capacity when the system and workload support it.

Feature Meaning MongoDB illustration
Flexible model Optional/nested fields can differ between records A phone and book store different specifications
Horizontal scale Data is partitioned across servers Sharding distributes a large collection

Key points

  • Flexible structure helps when product attributes or application requirements evolve, but validators and application checks should still protect required fields and types.
  • A shard/partition key determines data placement. A poor key can create a hot partition, so adding servers does not automatically remove every bottleneck.
  • Replication and sharding are different: replication maintains copies for redundancy, while sharding partitions data. Neither feature removes the need for backups or good indexing.

Example:

A catalogue may contain a phone document with screenInches: 6.1 and a book document with pages: 240, while both share id, name and price. As the catalogue grows, a suitable sharding design can distribute its records rather than forcing every record onto one server.

The example demonstrates evolving shape and distributed capacity, not a claim that all NoSQL products provide identical features or are always faster than SQL databases.

Conclusion: Flexible modelling addresses variation in data, and horizontal scaling addresses capacity. Both benefits depend on disciplined schema, query and partition-key design.

Short 6
Question
What is MongoDB? List any four features of MongoDB.
ShortUnit 11.1 Concepts of NoSQL — advantages & features
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database that stores BSON documents in collections. It supports nested values, queries and indexes, aggregation, replication and horizontal distribution.

Four major features can be summarized as follows:

Feature Explanation
Flexible document structure Records can contain optional fields, arrays and embedded documents
Indexed queries Appropriate indexes support equality, range and other searches
Replica sets Redundant copies and primary election support availability
Sharding A large dataset can be partitioned across servers

Key points

  • A standard collection uses _id as a unique identifier; additional unique indexes can protect application keys such as a roll number.
  • Schema flexibility is not an excuse for inconsistent types. Collection validation can enforce requirements even though records have optional attributes.
  • MongoDB supports atomic single-document writes and multi-document transactions; describing it as incapable of transactions is incorrect.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
// Document example, not a request to overwrite existing data.
const product = {
  id: 101, name: "Notebook", price: 80,
  tags: ["stationery"], specifications: {pages: 200}
};

This document keeps a product and its bounded specifications together. A query can inspect specifications.pages or an array value such as tags, rather than treating the record as opaque text. Indexes should follow actual query requirements instead of being added indiscriminately.

Conclusion: MongoDB combines a document model with query, availability and scaling features. Its suitability depends on access patterns and operational requirements, not just the NoSQL label.

Short 7
Question
Explain the need for NoSQL databases.
ShortUnit 11.1 Concepts of NoSQL — advantages & features
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: NoSQL databases are needed when an application's data model, evolving record shapes or distribution requirements are not conveniently served by a conventional relational design. They provide alternative models rather than a universal replacement for SQL.

Large catalogues, high-volume telemetry, direct key lookups and relationship traversals impose different requirements. A database should be selected after considering query patterns, integrity, latency, availability and maintenance effort.

Key points

  • Rapidly changing or nested records may fit document storage naturally, avoiding excessive table decomposition for information usually read as one unit.
  • Distributed workloads may benefit from partitioning and replication, although the chosen product's consistency and failure behavior must be understood.
  • Specialized models improve particular access patterns: key–value stores serve direct lookups, graph databases serve relationship traversal, and wide-column stores support planned partition/range access.

Example:

An e-commerce catalogue needs different specifications for phones, shoes and books. A document store can retain common fields while allowing category-specific attributes. A separate session cache may use key–value lookups. By contrast, a financial subsystem dominated by relational constraints and transactional reporting may still sensibly use a relational database.

The decision is not based solely on data size: relational databases can also scale, and some NoSQL designs make ad-hoc joins or integrity management more demanding.

Conclusion: The need for NoSQL arises from a mismatch between a workload and a data model or operational design. Choose it for a demonstrated requirement, not because SQL is assumed to be obsolete.

1.1.1 MongoDB datatypes

Short 8
Question
⭐⭐ What are the data types in MongoDB? List any three.
ShortUnit 11.1.1 MongoDB datatypes★ × 2
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: MongoDB stores values using BSON data types. Three valid examples are String, Boolean and Date; other important types include ObjectId, Int32, Int64, Double, Decimal128, arrays, embedded documents, binary data and null.

Type Example in mongosh Suitable use
String "Asha" Names or identifiers treated as text
Boolean true An active/inactive flag
Date ISODate("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z") An application timestamp

Key points

  • BSON has no separate Char or single-precision Float type. A character can be a one-character String; fractional values can use Double or Decimal128.
  • Choose numeric types by range and precision. An ordinary JavaScript Number cannot exactly represent every very large integer, and binary floating point is not exact decimal arithmetic.
  • Explicit null and a missing field are different states. A query {field: null} can match either; use a type/existence condition when the distinction matters.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
const student = {
  name: "Asha", active: true,
  enrolledAt: ISODate("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"),
  fee: NumberDecimal("199.95")
};

The date is stored as a BSON Date rather than merely as a text string, and the fee uses an explicit decimal representation. A Date stores an instant; timezone-sensitive display is a separate application concern.

Conclusion: Correct BSON typing makes filtering, sorting and arithmetic reliable. State both the type and an appropriate value when listing MongoDB data types.

1.1.2 Database creation and dropping database

Short 9
Question
What is the purpose of the db command in MongoDB? If no database is selected, what is the default database in MongoDB?
ShortUnit 11.1.2 Database creation and dropping database
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: In mongosh, db is the object representing the current database. Typing db displays the current database context; if neither the connection URI nor a use command selects another database, the normal default is test.

db is not a command that lists every database or creates a persistent database by itself. Its methods and collection properties provide access to operations in the current context.

Key points

  • db.getName() returns the current database name explicitly and is a useful check before running writes or destructive operations.
  • The interactive command use college changes the current database context, including when that database name does not yet exist.
  • Selection alone need not make a database appear in show dbs; creating a collection or writing data materializes it. A URI containing a different database name overrides the usual default context.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
// mongosh script-friendly equivalent of selecting another database.
db.getName();
db = db.getSiblingDB("college_practice");
db.getName();
db.createCollection("students");

The second getName() returns college_practice. Collection creation persists that database if necessary. If the collection already exists, creation may report a namespace-exists error; do not drop unrelated data just to repeat a demonstration.

Before typing db.dropDatabase(), confirm the selected name and obtain an appropriate backup. The meaning of db makes that verification important because the destructive method acts on the current database.

Conclusion: db identifies the shell's current database object, normally test when no other context is specified; selection and actual database creation are separate operations.

1.2 Create and drop collections

Short 10
Question
Differentiate between Collections and Tables.
ShortUnit 11.2 Create and drop collections
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: A collection is a group of BSON documents in MongoDB, whereas a table is a group of rows in a relational database. They play comparable grouping roles, but their record structures and relationship mechanisms differ.

Basis MongoDB collection Relational table
Record Document with field–value pairs Row with column values
Structure Optional/nested fields; validation can be configured Declared column schema and constraints
Identity Unique _id in a standard collection Declared primary-key constraint
Relationships Embedding, references and $lookup Foreign keys and joins
Common modelling focus Data commonly accessed together Entities and relational integrity

Key points

  • Collections can hold documents with different optional fields; this does not prevent the application from enforcing a consistent schema.
  • Arrays and embedded documents are central MongoDB modelling tools, while a relational model often separates repeating entities into related tables.
  • The contrast is not absolute: relational databases may support JSON columns, and MongoDB supports joins through aggregation and multi-document transactions.

Example:

A MongoDB student document can contain skills: ["HTML", "React"]. A normalized relational design might use one student row and two related skill rows. The first model retrieves the bounded skills with the student; the second makes individual relationships and relational constraints explicit.

Which is preferable depends on update frequency, query patterns and data-integrity requirements rather than the terminology alone.

Conclusion: Collection and table are useful analogies, not identical structures. Explain documents versus rows and the consequences for schema and relationship design.

1.2–1.3 Collections & CRUD operations

Short 11
Question
Write MongoDB query to remove all documents from a collection and to delete a collection.
ShortUnit 11.2–1.3 Collections & CRUD operations
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Use db.collection.deleteMany({}) to delete all documents while retaining the collection and indexes. Use db.collection.drop() to remove the collection itself, including its indexes. These are distinct, destructive operations.

Key points

  • An empty filter {} matches every document. It is not a request to delete nothing; a mistaken empty filter can erase the entire dataset.
  • deleteMany returns a result including deletedCount, whereas drop normally reports whether the collection was dropped. Check the returned result rather than assuming success.
  • Confirm the database with db.getName(), inspect the collection, and work only on disposable practice data or after appropriate authorization and backup.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
// DESTRUCTIVE: choose the one operation that matches your requirement.
db.getName();
db.students.countDocuments({});

// Option 1: retain the collection and its indexes.
db.students.deleteMany({});

// Option 2, a separate alternative: remove the collection itself.
// Do not run this if you only intended to empty it.
db.students.drop();

If the collection initially contains five documents, the first deletion should report deletedCount: 5, and a later count returns zero. Dropping the collection then removes its namespace and indexes, so future insertion would create a new collection without the previous index configuration unless it is recreated.

The commands are shown together for comparison, not as a recommendation that every cleanup should run both. db.dropDatabase() is broader still and is not required for either requested task.

Conclusion: Choose deleteMany({}) to empty a collection and drop() to remove it. The difference in retained structure is as important as the fact that both remove data.

Short 12
Question
Which method is used to add data in MongoDB? State the difference between insertOne and insertMany.
ShortUnit 11.2–1.3 Collections & CRUD operations
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: insertOne(document) and insertMany([documents]) are the modern MongoDB methods for adding documents. The first inserts one document; the second accepts an array and inserts several documents in one operation.

Feature insertOne insertMany
Input One document object An array of document objects
Insert identifiers insertedId insertedIds
Suitable use One new record A batch of records

Key points

  • Every document in a standard collection needs a unique _id; the driver/server normally generates one if it is omitted.
  • An acknowledged write result reports insertion information, but a follow-up query using an inserted identifier can verify the actual stored record.
  • Ordered bulk insertion stops at the first error by default. Earlier successful writes are not automatically rolled back, so do not mistake insertMany for an all-or-nothing transaction.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
db.students.insertOne({rollno: 1, name: "Asha"});
db.students.insertMany([
  {rollno: 2, name: "Ravi"},
  {rollno: 3, name: "Mira"}
]);
db.students.find({}, {_id: 0, rollno: 1, name: 1}).sort({rollno: 1});

Against a fresh collection, the query shows three students. A repeated logical roll number is prevented only if an appropriate unique index is created; MongoDB's default _id uniqueness is not automatically a uniqueness rule for every application field.

Conclusion: Select the insertion method according to the number of input documents, and check identifiers, acknowledgement and possible partial batch failure.

Short 13
Question
What is the difference between find() and findOne()?
ShortUnit 11.2–1.3 Collections & CRUD operations
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: find() returns a cursor over matching documents, while findOne() returns a single matching document or null. The different return types determine what operations can follow each call.

Feature find(filter, projection) findOne(filter, projection)
Return value Cursor Document or null
Result count Zero or more documents At most one document
Further cursor operations sort, limit, iteration Not cursor methods on the returned document

Key points

  • An empty filter selects all documents for find; it does not imply a meaningful “best” or “latest” record for findOne.
  • Projection controls returned fields, not whether the stored document still contains those fields. _id is normally included unless explicitly suppressed.
  • When a requirement specifies a rank or order, use an explicit sort, such as a descending marks sort followed by limit(1).

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
db.students.find({course: "BCA"}, {_id: 0, name: 1});
db.students.findOne({rollno: 1}, {_id: 0, name: 1});
db.students.find().sort({marks: -1, _id: 1}).limit(1);

The first query can return several names. The second returns the student with roll number 1 if present, otherwise null. The third deliberately selects a highest-mark record, using _id to break ties; it remains a cursor with at most one result.

Conclusion: Use find for a result set and findOne for one record, but never infer ranking from an unspecified retrieval order.

Short 14
Question
Differentiate upsert(), insert() and update() methods of MongoDB.
ShortUnit 11.2–1.3 Collections & CRUD operations
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: In MongoDB, insertion creates a document and updating changes matching documents. An upsert is an update-or-insert option: update a match, or insert when no document matches the filter.

Ambiguity note: The ordinary collection API does not provide a standalone upsert() method. The source's method name expresses a concept; modern code supplies {upsert: true} to an update or replacement operation. Legacy insert() and update() should be distinguished from current explicit one/many methods.

Operation Normal behavior Modern form
Insert Create new document(s) insertOne, insertMany
Update Modify matching document(s) updateOne, updateMany
Upsert Update a match or create a new record Update method with {upsert: true}

Key points

  • Without upsert, an update matching nothing inserts nothing; its matched count is zero.
  • The filter identifies the intended record, while modifiers such as $set describe field changes. A replacement document belongs with the appropriate replacement API.
  • Enforce uniqueness on the application's logical key, especially when concurrent upserts could otherwise introduce duplicates.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
db.students.updateOne(
  {rollno: 1},
  {$set: {name: "Asha", course: "BCA"}},
  {upsert: true}
);

An existing roll-number-1 record receives the named changes; otherwise MongoDB inserts a document based on the filter and update. Inspect matched/modified counts or the upsert identifier to see which path occurred.

Conclusion: Upsert is an option that changes an update's no-match behavior, not a separate ordinary collection method called upsert().

1.4 Operators & aggregation

Short 15
Question
⭐ Explain skip() and limit() methods in MongoDB.
ShortUnit 11.4 Operators & aggregation★ × 1
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: skip(n) omits the first n results of a MongoDB cursor, and limit(m) returns at most m results. They are commonly used with a stable sort to implement offset pagination.

For a one-based page number p and a positive page size s, the offset is (p − 1) × s. The variables count documents and pages; no physical measurement units are involved.

Key points

  • Define the sort order before interpreting “first” or “next.” A unique tie-breaker such as _id makes equal-value ordering deterministic.
  • limit(0) means no limit, not an empty result set. A positive limit larger than the available matches simply returns the available documents.
  • Large skips can be inefficient because earlier results still need to be traversed; range/keyset pagination is often more suitable for deep pages.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
db.students.find({}, {_id: 0, rollno: 1, name: 1})
  .sort({rollno: 1, _id: 1})
  .skip(10)
  .limit(5);

For page 3 and page size 5, (3 − 1) × 5 = 10. The query therefore returns positions 11–15 in the defined order, if that many students exist. It does not mean roll numbers 11–15: roll numbers might have gaps or start at another value.

If records are inserted or removed between page requests, offset-based pages may shift. Stable sorting helps ordering but does not freeze a changing dataset.

Conclusion: skip chooses an offset and limit caps a result count; pagination is meaningful only when its ordering and behavior under changing data are understood.

Short 16
Question
What is aggregation in MongoDB?
ShortUnit 11.4 Operators & aggregation
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Aggregation processes documents to filter, reshape and summarize data. MongoDB's aggregation pipeline passes the output of one stage to the next, allowing server-side calculations across many records.

A stage describes a processing step, while an accumulator describes a calculation within grouping. For example, $group forms groups and $sum adds values or counts their records.

Key points

  • $match filters documents, $project shapes fields, $group calculates group results, and $sort orders the output; stage order affects the result.
  • A field path such as "$category" refers to each document's field value. _id: null groups all input documents together instead of producing separate category groups.
  • Ordinary read-only pipelines do not modify source data. $merge and $out are explicit write-stage exceptions and must be used deliberately.

Example:

Suppose sales contain Book amounts 100 and 150, and Pen amount 20.

JavaScript / mongosh
db.sales.aggregate([
  {$group: {_id: "$category", total: {$sum: "$amount"}, count: {$sum: 1}}},
  {$sort: {_id: 1}}
]);

The results are Book with total 250 and count 2, and Pen with total 20 and count 1. $sum: "$amount" adds numeric amounts, whereas $sum: 1 counts documents. Validate numeric field types rather than assuming numeric-looking strings contribute as numbers.

Conclusion: Aggregation expresses multi-document processing as an ordered pipeline, keeping summary work near the data and making each filtering, grouping and calculation step explicit.

Unit 2 — Fundamentals of React.js

(16 questions)(16 questions)

2.1.1 Concepts of React

Short 17
Question
⭐⭐ What is JSX? What is its full form and why is JSX used with React?
ShortUnit 22.1.1 Concepts of React★ × 2
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: JSX, conventionally expanded as JavaScript XML, is a JavaScript syntax extension for describing user interfaces with markup-like expressions. React commonly uses it because it keeps the UI structure close to the JavaScript that supplies its data and behavior.

JSX is not a separate XML page and is not executed directly by a browser. A JSX-aware build tool transforms it into JavaScript element-creation calls. React can also be used without JSX, so it is a convenience rather than an absolute requirement.

Key points

  • JavaScript expressions appear inside braces, such as {student.name}. Statements such as for cannot be placed directly where JSX expects an expression.
  • Use JSX conventions such as className, close every tag, and wrap adjacent elements in one surrounding expression or Fragment.
  • Uppercase tags identify custom components, while lowercase tags identify native elements such as input, textarea and select.

Example:

React · JSX
function Greeting({name}) {
  return <section className="welcome">
    <h1>Hello, {name}</h1>
    <p>Welcome to React.</p>
  </section>;
}
const screen = <Greeting name="Asha" />;

In a configured React JSX application, rendering screen displays “Hello, Asha” and the welcome paragraph. Ordinary string values are rendered as text, rather than automatically being interpreted as HTML. Raw HTML injection is a separate operation with security implications.

Conclusion: JSX makes component trees readable and allows expressions to supply dynamic content, while a compilation step converts that notation into JavaScript React can use.

Short 18
Question
⭐ Differentiate between Real DOM and Virtual DOM.
ShortUnit 22.1.1 Concepts of React★ × 1
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: The real DOM is the browser's live object tree for a document. React's “Virtual DOM” is an informal description of the in-memory UI representations and reconciliation process used to decide which DOM changes to commit.

Basis Real DOM Virtual DOM model
Owner Browser React rendering machinery
Representation Live nodes and DOM interfaces JavaScript descriptions of desired UI
Visible effect DOM changes can cause style/layout/paint work Calculations alone do not paint the screen
Updating Node operations Render, compare/reconcile, then commit

Key points

  • A React render calculates a new UI description; it does not necessarily mean that every real DOM node will be replaced.
  • Stable component types and list keys help React preserve identity and state when comparing successive descriptions.
  • Virtual DOM is a rendering abstraction, not a guarantee that React is faster than every carefully written direct-DOM operation.

Example:

If a counter changes from 0 to 1, React can compute a new <p>Count: 1</p> description and update the relevant text during the commit. Unchanged surrounding inputs need not be discarded and recreated simply because the parent component rendered again.

The browser still performs the actual rendering after DOM changes. Expensive calculations inside components and unnecessarily large trees can remain performance problems, so profiling is more reliable than assuming the abstraction eliminates all work.

Conclusion: The virtual representation helps coordinate declarative updates, while the real DOM is the browser structure that ultimately produces the visible interface.

Short 19
Question
What is Virtual DOM?
ShortUnit 22.1.1 Concepts of React
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: The Virtual DOM is React's in-memory description of the UI it wants to render. After props or state change, React creates a new description and reconciles it with the previous one before committing necessary changes to the browser DOM.

This separates calculating the desired interface from modifying live nodes. Rendering can be repeated or restarted, so render logic should be pure rather than performing network requests or modifying external state.

Key points

  • Element types and keys help establish identity. Changing a component's type or key can cause React to recreate it and reset its local state.
  • A re-render does not automatically replace an entire page. React can preserve unaffected DOM nodes and update only the parts that need changing.
  • The Virtual DOM is not another visible browser document, and the term does not imply that all reconciliation work is free or always optimal.

Example:

React · JSX
function Score({value}) {
  return <p>Score: {value}</p>;
}
const firstView = <Score value={80} />;
const nextView = <Score value={85} />;

These values describe two versions of the same component type. In an application updating that component's prop, the displayed score changes to 85 while React may retain the paragraph node. The declarations alone do not mount anything; the application's root render or parent supplies the element to React.

Conclusion: The Virtual DOM model supports state-driven rendering by calculating and reconciling UI descriptions before committing changes to the real DOM.

Short 20
Question
List out advantages of React.
ShortUnit 22.1.1 Concepts of React
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: React's main advantages are reusable components, declarative rendering, clear one-way data flow, reusable stateful logic through hooks, and a broad development ecosystem.

Advantage Practical benefit
Components Reuse a tested UI unit in many places
Declarative views Describe output from state rather than manually synchronizing nodes
One-way data flow Make ownership and updates easier to trace
Hooks Reuse focused state/effect logic without class inheritance
Ecosystem Support testing, tooling, routing and richer rendering setups

Key points

  • Components provide boundaries for responsibilities and testing; making every tiny expression a component is not automatically beneficial.
  • React manages rendering, but a complete application may still need choices for routing, data access and other framework-level concerns.
  • Server rendering or hydration is possible with a suitable architecture, not an automatic consequence of importing React into a browser page.

Example:

A catalogue can define one ProductCard component and render it for each product with different props. Correcting its accessible button label or layout updates all uses of that component. A shared custom hook can encapsulate related loading behavior without forcing unrelated components to share one local state instance.

These advantages still require immutable updates, appropriate keys, accessible HTML and performance measurement. Poorly placed effects or tangled state ownership can make a React application difficult to maintain.

Conclusion: React is valuable for composing predictable, reusable interactive interfaces; its advantages come from disciplined component and state design rather than an automatic performance guarantee.

2.1.2 Using React with HTML

Short 21
Question
What is create-react-app? Why is it used?
ShortUnit 22.1.2 Using React with HTML
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Create React App (CRA) is a historical scaffolding tool that generated a React project with JSX compilation, a development server and a production build configuration. It reduced the amount of manual Babel and bundler setup needed for a new application.

Ambiguity note: CRA was deprecated for new applications in February 2025. The command remains the expected historical syllabus answer, but it is not the preferred starting point for a new project today.

Key points

  • CRA generated a project structure and configured tooling; it was not the React library itself or a browser API.
  • Its traditional development command was npm start inside the generated directory, while npm run build created production assets.
  • New learning projects can use a current tool such as Vite; larger applications may benefit from a recommended React framework. The choice depends on requirements rather than the name of the editor.

Example:

Terminal commands
# Historical CRA workflow, retained for the syllabus.
npx create-react-app myapp
cd myapp
npm start

The command creates a folder named myapp; after changing into that folder, the development server prints a browser address. Initial dependency installation needs network access, and the installed tooling requires a compatible Node.js version. A server running successfully does not by itself deploy the app publicly or add a backend.

Conclusion: CRA standardized early React project setup, but an accurate answer now distinguishes its historical purpose and commands from current project-creation recommendations.

Short 22
Question
Write the steps to create and run a React application in VS Code.
ShortUnit 22.1.2 Using React with HTML
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: To create and run a React application in VS Code, install a Node.js version supported by the chosen build tool, scaffold a React project, install its dependencies and start its development server from the integrated terminal.

VS Code is the editor, not the React runtime or package manager. The commands below use Vite for a current client-side learning project; commands differ for other scaffolds.

Key points

  • Use a new project directory, check the Node/npm versions, and run subsequent commands from the generated project's root.
  • Initial package download requires internet access. Once installed, the local development server compiles JSX and reports the actual browser URL to open.
  • Edit src/App.jsx to change the UI. The editor's code . command is optional: if unavailable, open the directory through VS Code's File menu.

Example:

Terminal commands
npm create vite@latest myapp -- --template react
cd myapp
npm install
code .
npm run dev

Open the address printed by the final command, change the heading in src/App.jsx, and save. The development preview should update. Stop the foreground server with Ctrl+C when finished. npm run build checks/builds production assets but does not automatically publish them to a hosting service.

Ambiguity note: Older question papers may expect npx create-react-app myapp followed by npm start. CRA is deprecated for new apps; do not interchange its script names with Vite's without checking the generated package.json.

Conclusion: Correct setup requires compatible tooling, the right working directory and the scaffold's actual start command, not simply opening a JSX file directly in a browser.

2.1.3 Components & props

Short 23
Question
⭐⭐⭐ What are props in React JS?
ShortUnit 22.1.3 Components & props★ × 3
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Props are read-only inputs passed from a parent into a React component. They configure what a component displays or how it reports events, without allowing the receiving component to mutate its parent's data.

A function component receives one props object and can destructure its fields. Props can contain text, numbers, objects, JSX or callback functions; nested JSX is provided through the children prop.

Key points

  • Read-only means that the child must not assign to received props or mutate nested objects. The parent can supply different values on a later render.
  • A callback prop lets the child request a change from the owner rather than directly changing the owner's state.
  • Props and state both affect rendering, but props come from outside the component while local state is managed through React's state APIs.

Example:

React · JSX
function Student({name, course}) {
  return <p>{name} studies {course}.</p>;
}
const screen = <Student name="Asha" course="BCA" />;

When rendered in a configured React application, the output is “Asha studies BCA.” Another instance can receive Ravi and BBA without changing the component definition. A number such as marks={85} uses braces; marks="85" supplies a string instead.

A key used for list identity is special React metadata, not an ordinary prop the child can read as props.key; pass a separate identifier if the child needs it.

Conclusion: Props provide an explicit parent-to-child interface and support reusable components while preserving clear ownership of data and changes.

Short 24
Question
What are props in React? Differentiate between state and props.
ShortUnit 22.1.3 Components & props
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Props are inputs provided to a component by its parent, while state is changing data owned by the component. Both influence rendering, but the receiving child must treat props as read-only and update state only through React's update APIs.

Basis Props State
Owner Parent or caller Component that declares it
How it changes Parent supplies new values Setter, reducer dispatch or class setState
Typical role Configuration and external data Local memory such as an edited field or counter
Direct mutation Not permitted as an update pattern Also not a valid update pattern

Key points

  • A parent may pass its own state as a child's prop; “state” and “prop” describe ownership at that boundary, not different primitive data types.
  • Copying a prop into useState initializes state but does not automatically keep it synchronized with later prop changes.
  • Shared values should normally have one owner, often a common parent, rather than independent copies that can disagree.

Example:

React · JSX
import {useState} from "react";
function Counter({initial}) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(initial);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(c => c + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}
const screen = <Counter initial={5} />;

The initial prop starts the local count at 5. A click changes the state to 6; it does not rewrite the parent's initial prop. If the parent later changes initial, this already-mounted counter is not automatically reset.

Conclusion: Props communicate external inputs, whereas state stores component-owned memory. Clear ownership prevents accidental mutation and synchronization errors.

Short 25
Question
What is the use of render() in ReactJS?
ShortUnit 22.1.3 Components & props
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: In a React class component, render() returns a UI description derived from this.props and this.state. React calls it as part of rendering; the method should calculate output without performing external side effects.

The method returns React-renderable content, not a command to manually replace the whole document. Function components return their output directly and do not define an instance render() method.

Key points

  • Keep render() pure: do not start network requests, change global data or unconditionally call setState inside it.
  • A component may return JSX, a Fragment, text, null or other supported renderable values; adjacent JSX expressions need appropriate grouping.
  • The root API createRoot(...).render(<App />) mounts/updates a React root and is different from a class component's own render() method.

Example:

React · JSX
import {Component} from "react";
class Welcome extends Component {
  render() {
    return <h1>Hello, {this.props.name}</h1>;
  }
}
const screen = <Welcome name="Asha" />;

Rendering this element in a configured application displays “Hello, Asha.” If the parent supplies a new name, React can invoke rendering again and reconcile the result. It should remain safe to calculate the output more than once, because rendering may be restarted or repeated by React.

Place subscriptions or fetching in appropriate lifecycle/effect logic and clean them up when necessary rather than embedding them in this calculation.

Conclusion: render() is the pure UI-description method of a class component, not a general-purpose place for initialization, requests or state-changing side effects.

2.2.2 Conditional statements, operators & lists

Short 26
Question
What is a list?
ShortUnit 22.2.2 Conditional statements, operators & lists
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: A list in React is a sequence of related UI items rendered from a collection, commonly by using an array's map() method to create JSX elements. It represents data-driven repetition rather than manually duplicating the same markup.

The resulting elements are normally placed inside a container such as <ul> with <li> children, though other accessible structures can be used when appropriate.

Key points

  • Give each directly returned sibling a stable key, preferably a persistent record ID, so React can track its identity through insertions, deletion and reordering.
  • Keys need to be unique among those siblings, not globally across the application. Random values or changing indexes can cause unnecessary remounting or incorrect state association.
  • map returns a new array of results; rendering an empty array produces no list items. Provide an explicit empty-state message when that improves usability.

Example:

React · JSX
function StudentList() {
  const students = [{id: 1, name: "Asha"}, {id: 2, name: "Ravi"}];
  return <ul>{students.map(student =>
    <li key={student.id}>{student.name}</li>
  )}</ul>;
}

The output is a two-item list containing Asha and Ravi. If each item later contains an editable field, a stable ID helps preserve the correct field state when students move. The key is special React metadata; pass a separate studentId prop if a child component needs the ID as data.

Conclusion: React lists convert collections into repeated UI, and stable keys are essential for preserving item identity as that collection changes.

Short 27
Question
What is a spread operator?
ShortUnit 22.2.2 Conditional statements, operators & lists
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: JavaScript spread syntax ... expands iterable values in arrays/function calls or copies enumerable own properties into an object literal. React commonly uses object or array spread to create updated state values without mutating the previous ones.

Spread is a language feature, not a React-specific database or event operator. The identical three-dot notation can also represent rest syntax in a parameter/destructuring position; the context determines the operation.

Key points

  • In an object literal, later properties replace earlier properties with the same name, so {...person, age: 21} copies the old fields and then changes age.
  • The copy is shallow: nested objects or arrays still share references unless those changed levels are copied separately.
  • Copying does not itself update React state. Pass the new value to the state setter, preferably using a functional updater when the update depends on previous state.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
const student = {name: "Asha", course: "BCA"};
const revised = {...student, course: "BBA"};
const first = [1, 2];
const extended = [...first, 3];

student.course stays BCA, while revised.course is BBA; extended becomes [1, 2, 3] without changing first. If student also held address: {city: "Ahmedabad"}, copying the outer object would not independently copy that address.

For nested React state, update the required nesting levels rather than assuming spread performs a deep clone.

Conclusion: Spread simplifies expansion and immutable update patterns, but it is shallow and must be combined with the correct React setter and ownership rules.

Short 28
Question
How do we conditionally render statements in the JSX part of a React component?
ShortUnit 22.2.2 Conditional statements, operators & lists
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Conditional rendering chooses which UI to return based on a condition. Inside JSX braces, use expressions such as the conditional operator condition ? A : B or logical &&; ordinary if and switch statements belong in the surrounding JavaScript function.

A component can also return early or return null to omit its own rendered output. The chosen technique should make the condition and resulting UI clear rather than forcing complex logic into one expression.

Key points

  • Use a ternary when both true and false alternatives need explicit UI, and && when only the true case needs content.
  • Use a Boolean condition such as count > 0; {count && <p>...</p>} can display the number 0 because JavaScript returns the falsy operand.
  • Hiding or omitting a client-side component is not an authorization check. Protect sensitive data before delivering it to the browser.

Example:

React · JSX
function Status({loggedIn, count}) {
  return <div>
    {loggedIn ? <p>Welcome</p> : <p>Please log in</p>}
    {count > 0 && <p>{count} messages</p>}
  </div>;
}

With loggedIn true and count 2, the component displays Welcome and 2 messages. With false and zero, it displays only Please log in—no unintended “0” text. This example assumes the parent supplies a Boolean and a numeric count with the intended types.

Conclusion: Use expressions inside JSX and statements outside it, taking care that the condition's value and type produce the intended visible output.

2.2.3 React events

Short 29
Question
What is an event in ReactJS?
ShortUnit 22.2.3 React events
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: A React event represents an interaction such as a click, input change, form submission or focus change. An event handler is a function passed to a camelCase JSX event prop, such as onClick or onSubmit.

React provides an event object exposing useful properties and methods. The handler normally updates state or performs the requested interaction; React then renders from the resulting state rather than requiring manual DOM text updates.

Key points

  • Pass the function, as in onClick={handleClick}, rather than invoking it during rendering with onClick={handleClick()}.
  • event.target is the originating element; event.currentTarget is the element whose handler is executing, which matters when nested content receives a click.
  • preventDefault() cancels a cancelable browser action, while stopPropagation() changes event propagation. They solve different problems and returning false is not the React substitute for either.

Example:

React · JSX
import {useState} from "react";
function ClickCounter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button type="button" onClick={() => setCount(c => c + 1)}>
    Clicked {count} times
  </button>;
}

Initially the button says Clicked 0 times; two activations produce Clicked 2 times. The functional setter safely calculates from the pending previous value, and the native button remains keyboard-accessible.

Conclusion: React event handling connects user actions to explicit functions and state updates, with browser-default behavior and propagation controlled separately when required.

2.3.1 Handling forms — event.target

Short 30
Question
⭐⭐ Explain event.target.name in ReactJS.
ShortUnit 22.3.1 Handling forms — event.target★ × 2
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: event.target.name reads the name attribute of the control that originated an event. It identifies which form field changed; it does not return the entered value, the control's ID or the event type.

A shared handler can combine this name with event.target.value to update the matching property of a form-state object. This reduces repeated handlers while preserving explicit field names.

Key points

  • Set each input's name to the intended state property; without a meaningful name, the handler cannot reliably identify that property.
  • Use a computed property such as [name] and a copied object to update one field without mutating state or deleting unrelated fields.
  • Accept only expected field names. Checkboxes normally use checked, and file controls use files, so a text-value handler is not automatically suitable for every input type.

Example:

React · JSX
import {useState} from "react";
function EmailField() {
  const [form, setForm] = useState({email: ""});
  function change(event) {
    const {name, value} = event.target;
    if (name !== "email") return;
    setForm(previous => ({...previous, [name]: value}));
  }
  return <input name="email" type="email" value={form.email} onChange={change} />;
}

When the user types [email protected], the name is email and the value is the entered address. The handler uses the first as a key and the second as its new data; the two properties have different roles.

Conclusion: event.target.name identifies a field and is particularly useful for allowlisted shared form handlers that update state immutably.

Short 31
Question
What is the use of event.target.value?
ShortUnit 22.3.1 Handling forms — event.target
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: event.target.value reads the current value of the control that originated an event. In a controlled React text input, the change handler stores that value in state, and the value prop sends the state back to the displayed control.

This creates an explicit state-driven editing cycle. The property is different from event.target.name, which identifies the field, and from currentTarget, which identifies the element whose handler is running.

Key points

  • Text-control values are strings, including many numeric input values. Validate and convert only when the application actually requires a number, taking empty input into account.
  • Checkboxes use checked for their Boolean state, and file inputs expose selected files through files; blindly reading value for every control is incorrect.
  • Initialize a controlled text state to a string such as "" rather than switching later from undefined to a controlled value.

Example:

React · JSX
import {useState} from "react";
function NameField() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  return <section>
    <label>Name <input value={name}
      onChange={event => setName(event.target.value)} /></label>
    <p>Hello, {name || "visitor"}</p>
  </section>;
}

Typing Asha updates the state and greeting to Hello, Asha. Clearing the input restores the visitor fallback. React renders the supplied string as text, but displaying it safely is not the same thing as validating it for a backend operation.

Conclusion: event.target.value supplies a control's current text-like value; correct handling also requires the right control property, type conversion and state initialization.

2.4 Hooks

Short 32
Question
What are Hooks in React JS?
ShortUnit 22.4 Hooks
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Hooks are React functions that let function components use features such as state, effects, context and refs. Custom hooks combine reusable stateful logic and conventionally have names beginning with use.

Hook Main purpose
useState Component-owned state and its setter
useEffect Synchronization with external systems after a commit
useRef Stable mutable reference without triggering rendering
useContext Read a supplied context value

Key points

  • Call ordinary hooks at the top level of a function component or another custom hook, not inside loops, conditions, class methods or event handlers.
  • A custom hook shares logic, not an automatic single shared state instance. Separate calls normally have separate state unless they explicitly use a shared mechanism.
  • Effects need correct dependencies and cleanup for ongoing work. Hooks do not make direct mutation or side effects during render safe.

Example:

React · JSX
import {useState} from "react";
function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(c => c + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}

The first render displays 0; a click queues a new count and a later render displays 1. The click handler invokes the setter returned by the hook; it does not call useState inside the event. The rules above concern ordinary syllabus hooks; newer React's special use API has separate rules.

Conclusion: Hooks give function components persistent behavior through React's lifecycle and rendering system, provided their call order, dependencies and update rules are respected.

Unit 3 — Fundamentals of Angular

(5 questions)(5 questions)

3.1 Concepts and characteristics of Angular

Short 33
Question
⭐ What is AngularJS? Explain any two of its features.
ShortUnit 33.1 Concepts and characteristics of Angular★ × 1
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: AngularJS is the original 1.x JavaScript front-end framework for building dynamic browser applications, including single-page applications. It is distinct from modern TypeScript-oriented Angular. Two important AngularJS features are data binding and dependency injection.

Feature Meaning Benefit
Data binding Connects scope data and a template, including editable ng-model controls Reduces manual view synchronization
Dependency injection Supplies registered dependencies such as $http to consumers Reduces direct construction and supports testing

Key points

  • Directives such as ng-app, ng-model and ng-repeat give HTML application behavior; they are interpreted by AngularJS rather than by plain HTML alone.
  • Controllers prepare view data/actions, while services can hold reusable logic; a controller should not become a collection of unrelated manual DOM operations.
  • AngularJS official support ended in January 2022. Its historical features remain syllabus material, but it is not the current Angular framework under a different spelling.

Example:

Inside an initialized AngularJS application, <input ng-model="student.name"> and <p>{{student.name}}</p> stay connected through binding. Typing Asha changes the displayed paragraph without explicitly finding and rewriting that paragraph's DOM node. A controller can request an injected data service instead of constructing a global dependency itself.

The example assumes the AngularJS library and application module are already loaded; attributes alone do not download the framework.

Conclusion: AngularJS combined declarative templates, data binding and dependency injection to simplify dynamic views, but its 1.x APIs and support status must be distinguished from modern Angular.

3.1.1.2 Modules

Short 34
Question
Explain the meaning of var ngApp = angular.module('myApp', []); with respect to AngularJS.
ShortUnit 33.1.1.2 Modules
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: var ngApp = angular.module('myApp', []); creates an AngularJS module named myApp and stores its module API object in the JavaScript variable ngApp. The empty array declares that this module has no additional module dependencies.

The module is a container for controller, service, directive and other registrations. It is not itself a DOM element, a controller instance or a modern Angular @NgModule class.

Key points

  • Supplying the second argument creates the module; calling angular.module('myApp') without the array retrieves the existing registration.
  • Dependencies can be listed as names, such as ['ngRoute'], provided their corresponding scripts and modules are available.
  • Attach the module to an automatically bootstrapped region with ng-app="myApp"; keep the spelling identical to the registered name.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
// AngularJS 1.8.x must be loaded before this script.
var ngApp = angular.module('myApp', []);
ngApp.controller('GreetingController', function() {
  this.message = 'Hello from myApp';
});

A template region using ng-controller="GreetingController as vm" can then display {{vm.message}}. The output is Hello from myApp after AngularJS bootstraps and links the template.

If another file needs the existing module, it should retrieve it with angular.module('myApp'), not create it again with an empty array. Re-creation can reset registrations and cause apparently missing controllers or services.

Conclusion: The statement names and creates an application module, declares dependencies and provides an object through which its components can be registered.

3.2 Routing, navigation & environment setup

Short 35
Question
⭐ Explain ngRoute.
ShortUnit 33.2 Routing, navigation & environment setup★ × 1
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: ngRoute is AngularJS's optional client-side routing module. It maps application URL paths to templates and controllers, placing the selected view in an ng-view region without a complete browser-document reload for each navigation.

Routing organizes a single-page application's views; it is not a substitute for a backend API, authorization rules or persistent data storage.

Key points

  • Load a local matching-version angular-route.min.js after angular.min.js, then declare ['ngRoute'] when creating the application module.
  • Configure paths with $routeProvider.when() and a fallback with .otherwise() during module configuration.
  • $routeParams exposes captured path parameters. Validate and authorize any identifier before using it to access protected backend data.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
angular.module('routeDemo', ['ngRoute'])
  .config(['$routeProvider', function(routes) {
    routes.when('/home', {template: '<h1>Home</h1>'})
      .when('/about', {template: '<h1>About</h1>'})
      .otherwise({redirectTo: '/home'});
  }]);

With an ng-app="routeDemo" root and <main ng-view></main>, navigating to the configured home path displays Home inside that main element. In a default AngularJS 1.8 hash-prefix setup, a link can use #!/home. HTML5 history mode has additional server fallback requirements.

Ambiguity note: Modern Angular uses @angular/router, Router and <router-outlet>; those APIs are not interchangeable with AngularJS ngRoute.

Conclusion: ngRoute coordinates AngularJS view navigation through configured URL-to-template mappings and an ng-view placeholder.

Short 36
Question
⭐⭐ What is the use of $routeProvider service of ngRoute?
ShortUnit 33.2 Routing, navigation & environment setup★ × 2
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: $routeProvider configures the routes used by AngularJS's ngRoute module. It associates paths with template/controller definitions and provides fallback behavior for paths that do not match a configured route.

Ambiguity note: Although the question calls it a service, it is a configuration-time provider. The runtime service $route manages the active route, while $routeParams supplies captured parameters.

Key points

  • Use .when(path, definition) to register a route and .otherwise(...) to specify a redirect or fallback.
  • A route definition can use template or templateUrl, a controller and optional resolved dependencies; its content is inserted into ng-view.
  • Load the routing script and declare the ngRoute module dependency before attempting to inject $routeProvider into a .config(...) function.

Example:

JavaScript / mongosh
angular.module('app', ['ngRoute'])
  .config(['$routeProvider', function(routes) {
    routes.when('/home', {template: '<h2>Home</h2>'})
      .otherwise({redirectTo: '/home'});
  }]);

In a bootstrapped application containing ng-view, the home route displays the heading Home. An unmatched path redirects to the configured home path instead of leaving navigation undefined. Array-style dependency annotation remains correct when a minifier renames the JavaScript parameter routes.

Route configuration itself does not verify user permissions. Server-side authorization must protect the data behind a route even if the navigation link is hidden.

Conclusion: $routeProvider establishes AngularJS routing rules during configuration; view activation and parameter access are handled by related runtime services.

Short 37
Question
How can you integrate Angular JS with HTML?
ShortUnit 33.2 Routing, navigation & environment setup
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Integrate AngularJS with HTML by loading its library, defining an application module and marking the application root with ng-app. AngularJS then compiles directives and links expressions inside that root to a scope.

For an offline example, keep a trusted AngularJS 1.8.x angular.min.js beside the example HTML. This runtime prerequisite belongs to the study example; the question-bank reader itself does not load AngularJS.

Key points

  • Match the module name in angular.module(...) to the ng-app attribute, and register application code before automatic bootstrapping completes.
  • Directives such as ng-model and ng-bind add behavior only after the library runs; they are not native HTML features that work by themselves.
  • Use controllers/services for substantial application logic and avoid compiling untrusted user text as a template.

Example:

HTML · study example
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" ng-app="demo">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>AngularJS integration</title></head>
<body>
  <h1>Expression example</h1><p>{{2 + 3}}</p>
  <script src="angular.min.js"></script>
  <script>angular.module("demo", []);</script>
</body></html>

Opening the example with the local library available displays 5 in the paragraph after bootstrapping. If the library path is wrong, the expression may remain unevaluated and application behavior will not run. If the named module is missing, bootstrapping reports a module error rather than inventing it automatically.

Conclusion: AngularJS integration requires both a loaded framework/module and a declared HTML application region; matching names and script order are essential.

Unit 4 — Angular Features

(8 questions)(8 questions)

4.1.2 Component lifecycle hooks

Short 38
Question
Explain ngOnInit and ngOnChanges.
ShortUnit 44.1.2 Component lifecycle hooks
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: In modern Angular, ngOnInit() initializes a component once after its initial input values are set. ngOnChanges(changes: SimpleChanges) responds when Angular detects changes to bound inputs, including their first assignment.

Hook Frequency Information available
ngOnInit Once per component instance Initialized input properties
ngOnChanges Initial and later detected input changes Previous/current values and first-change flag

Key points

  • The first ngOnChanges runs before ngOnInit when Angular assigns bound inputs; the order matters for input-dependent setup.
  • SimpleChanges maps input names to SimpleChange records. Each record exposes previousValue, currentValue and firstChange.
  • Mutating an object's nested property without replacing its reference may not produce an input-change notification; neither hook is an automatic deep-difference detector.

Example:

A child component receives [studentName]="name". If the parent initially supplies Asha, Angular first reports that input change and then runs the child's initialization. Changing the bound value to Ravi later can run ngOnChanges again, but does not rerun ngOnInit on that same instance. Removing and recreating the child creates a new instance with a new initialization cycle.

Ambiguity note: These are modern Angular names; AngularJS component hooks use $onInit and $onChanges and must not be substituted into the same code.

Conclusion: Use ngOnInit for one-time instance setup and ngOnChanges for explicit reactions to changed inputs, with correct expectations about order and object identity.

4.2 Angular directives

Short 39
Question
What is ng-init?
ShortUnit 44.2 Angular directives
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: ng-init is an AngularJS directive that evaluates an initialization expression in the scope where it is linked. It can assign simple initial values used by nearby expressions and directives.

It does not create or bootstrap an application, and it does not replace the ng-app directive or module registration. Its expression runs in the template's AngularJS context rather than as an independent server-side operation.

Key points

  • Multiple small assignments can be separated with semicolons in the initialization expression, and values can include numbers, strings, objects or arrays.
  • Initialization is associated with the linked scope/view. Recreating a view can lead to initialization again, so do not place irreversible operations there.
  • For real applications, initialize business data in controllers/components or services; lengthy template assignments make logic harder to test and maintain.

Example:

HTML · study example
<!-- This fragment belongs inside an initialized AngularJS application. -->
<section ng-init="quantity=2; price=50">
  <p>Quantity: {{quantity}}</p>
  <p>Total: {{quantity * price}}</p>
</section>

The displayed quantity is 2 and the total is 100. The expression multiplies two numeric values; assigning the text "two" would not provide the same arithmetic behavior. This small example explains the directive without recommending that a production catalogue be hardcoded into HTML.

Conclusion: ng-init evaluates scope-local initialization, useful for limited demonstrations or template cases, while substantial data setup belongs in maintainable application logic.

Short 40
Question
⭐⭐ Explain ng-show and ng-hide.
ShortUnit 44.2 Angular directives★ × 2
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: In AngularJS, ng-show shows an element when its expression is truthy, while ng-hide hides it when its expression is truthy. Both control visibility without removing the element from the DOM.

Condition value ng-show="visible" ng-hide="visible"
true Visible Hidden
false Hidden Visible

Key points

  • Both directives toggle the ng-hide CSS class; the hidden subtree, associated state and watchers can remain present.
  • ng-if is different: it creates/removes its block and child scope, potentially resetting DOM-local state when recreated.
  • Pass an expression directly rather than wrapping it in interpolation. Boolean false is not the same as the nonempty string "false", which is truthy.

Example:

HTML · study example
<!-- Fragment inside an initialized AngularJS application. -->
<div ng-init="visible=false">
  <label><input type="checkbox" ng-model="visible">Show help</label>
  <p ng-show="visible">The help paragraph is visible.</p>
  <p ng-hide="visible">Help is currently hidden.</p>
</div>

Initially only the second paragraph is shown. Selecting the checkbox shows the first and hides the second; clearing it reverses the behavior. This uses one Boolean property as the single source of truth.

A user can still inspect hidden content in developer tools, so hiding sensitive text is not authorization. Protected data should not be delivered to an unauthorized browser in the first place.

Conclusion: ng-show and ng-hide are opposite visibility conditions that retain DOM content; choose them rather than ng-if when preserving that content is intentional.

4.3 Angular data binding

Short 41
Question
⭐⭐⭐ What are AngularJS expressions? Explain with example.
ShortUnit 44.3 Angular data binding★ × 3
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: AngularJS expressions evaluate data in the current scope and produce values used by a template. They commonly appear inside {{ ... }} interpolation or directly in directive attributes such as ng-bind="student.name".

Expressions support property access, arithmetic, strings and filter application. They are not unrestricted JavaScript programs: general declarations and flow-control statements are not inserted as template expressions, and ordinary browser globals are not directly available in the same way.

Key points

  • Interpolation uses double curly braces; a directive such as ng-bind takes the expression itself rather than an extra pair of interpolation braces.
  • Keep expressions small and side-effect-free because AngularJS may evaluate them repeatedly during its digest/binding process.
  • Never compile untrusted user text as an AngularJS expression or template. Tolerant handling of some missing values is not a security boundary.

Example:

HTML · study example
<!-- Fragment inside an initialized AngularJS application. -->
<div ng-init="first='Robert'; last='Desoza'; marks=80">
  <p>{{first + ' ' + last}}</p>
  <p>Revised marks: {{marks + 5}}</p>
</div>

The output is Robert Desoza and Revised marks: 85. The second expression calculates display output; it does not assign 85 back into the marks model, which remains 80. Assigning state and deriving display values are different operations.

Conclusion: AngularJS expressions connect model values to readable template output, provided their syntax, scope and side-effect limitations are respected.

Short 42
Question
What is data binding in Angular JS?
ShortUnit 44.3 Angular data binding
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Data binding in AngularJS connects application model values with their view representation. Interpolation or ng-bind displays model data, while ng-model on a supported control can also carry edits from the view back into the model.

AngularJS's digest mechanism checks watched expressions and updates affected bindings. This reduces the need to manually find and rewrite each related DOM element after every edit.

Key points

  • Model-to-view output can use {{name}} or ng-bind="name"; neither makes an ordinary paragraph an editable form control.
  • ng-model includes parsing, formatting and validation behavior for controls. Invalid draft input may not be written as a valid model value under normal settings.
  • Binding synchronizes UI and in-memory data; it does not automatically save to a database, authorize a user or make data permanent across reloads.

Example:

HTML · study example
<!-- Fragment inside an initialized AngularJS application. -->
<section ng-init="student={name:'Robert'}">
  <label>Name <input ng-model="student.name"></label>
  <p>Hello, <span ng-bind="student.name"></span></p>
</section>

Initially the input and greeting show Robert. Typing Asha changes the model through ng-model and updates the span through ng-bind. A controller assignment to student.name can also update both views; the output does not need a second independently maintained name variable.

Use object property paths to make ownership clearer when nested scopes are present, and move significant initialization into a controller or service.

Conclusion: Binding coordinates model and view state, but persistence, validation policy and security still require explicit application and backend design.

4.4 Angular pipes (filters)

Short 43
Question
What is currency filter in Angular JS?
ShortUnit 44.4 Angular pipes (filters)
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: AngularJS's currency filter formats a numeric value as a currency string using locale rules. It supports an optional currency symbol and an optional number of fractional digits; it is a presentation transformation, not an exchange-rate calculation.

The syntax is {{ amount | currency:currencySymbol:fractionSize }}. The pipe invokes the filter and the colon-separated arguments customize its display.

Key points

  • With the standard en-US locale, grouping, decimal separators and symbol placement follow that locale even if a different symbol such as ₹ is supplied.
  • Changing the symbol does not change the underlying numeric amount or convert rupees to dollars; real currency conversion needs an exchange rate and a defined rounding policy.
  • Store and calculate money using an appropriate numeric representation and currency unit rather than treating a formatted display string as the canonical amount.

Example:

HTML · study example
<!-- Fragment inside an initialized AngularJS application. -->
<div ng-init="amount=1234.5">
  <p>{{amount | currency:'₹':2}}</p>
  <p>Unformatted amount: {{amount}}</p>
</div>

With the stated locale, the first paragraph shows ₹1,234.50, while the second shows the original numeric value 1234.5. The filter pads fractional digits for display; it does not mutate amount into a string containing the symbol or separators. Other locales may produce different grouping and symbol placement.

Conclusion: The currency filter makes monetary output readable, but currency identity, arithmetic precision and conversion remain separate application responsibilities.

4.5 Angular forms & validation

Short 44
Question
What is $dirty and $touched states in AngularJS form validation?
ShortUnit 44.5 Angular forms & validation
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: $dirty indicates that an AngularJS control has been changed through the view or marked dirty through its API. $touched indicates that the control has lost focus, normally through a blur event. They describe interaction history, not whether the value is valid.

State Opposite Typical transition
$dirty $pristine User edits the value
$touched $untouched User focuses and then leaves the control

Key points

  • A control can be touched but pristine if the user focuses it and leaves without editing; the flags therefore cannot be substituted for each other.
  • A dirty field can be valid, and an untouched required field can be invalid. Validation state is represented separately by $valid, $invalid and $error.
  • Returning to the initial value does not automatically make a field pristine. Explicit reset APIs can reset interaction flags when appropriate for the workflow.

Example:

In a named form studentForm with a required email control named email, an error condition can be studentForm.email.$touched && studentForm.email.$invalid. Focusing and blurring the empty field then reveals an error even though the user did not type. An alternative based only on $dirty would not reveal that same unchanged-empty-field case.

A submit attempt can be included with studentForm.$submitted so that all missing required fields receive feedback when the user tries to continue.

Conclusion: $dirty tracks editing and $touched tracks focus departure; combining interaction flags with independent validity flags produces better-timed validation feedback.

Short 45
Question
State the purpose of AngularJS directives $invalid and $dirty.
ShortUnit 44.5 Angular forms & validation
▶
Answer:

Definition / direct answer: $invalid reports that validation has failed for an AngularJS form or control, while $dirty reports that a value has been edited through the view or marked dirty. They answer different questions: “Is it valid?” and “Has it been changed?”

Ambiguity note: The question calls these directives, but they are state properties of AngularJS form/control controllers, not directives themselves. Directives such as required or ng-pattern establish rules that affect those states.

Property Purpose Example
$invalid Report failed validation A required email field is empty
$dirty Record view-edit history The user has typed in the field

Key points

  • An untouched required field can already be invalid; validity does not depend on whether the user has interacted with it.
  • A dirty field can contain a perfectly valid value, so $dirty must not be used as a synonym for an error.
  • Use $error to identify particular failed rules, and combine validity with $dirty, $touched or form $submitted to control feedback timing.

Example:

For a form f with a control named email, f.email.$invalid && (f.email.$dirty || f.$submitted) displays a validation message after an edit or submit attempt. Correcting the address removes the error even though $dirty remains true. Disabling a submit button with f.$invalid can help users, but a guarded submit handler and server-side validation are still necessary.

Conclusion: $invalid represents validation failure and $dirty represents editing history. Their distinction is essential for correct form logic and does not create a security boundary.
